sections.h: Working translation (31 October 2026) for the app of Mother Rosa’s writings — to be checked by a native-speaker reviewer. The signs [?] mark passages that are uncertain or damaged in the original.

This collection brings together the prayers of Mother Rosa kept in the archive «03 · CARISMA FSA». They fall into two groups.

I. Prayers of Mother Rosa — nineteen texts, from the collection «Preghiere di Madre Rosa» (folder «Pregare con Madre Rosa»); the other two copies of the same booklet («Preghiere di M.R.», «Alcune preghiere di Madre Rosa») have the same text, apart from minor variants. They are not found in the editions of the Memoirs (2026 typeset edition), the Letters (2025 ed.), Travagli e Conforti or the Conferences: they come from loose writings. No. 11 is described as a «keepsake written in her own hand» (1899); no. 19, To Saint Anne, is presented in the booklet «Spiritualità di Avvento» as «a writing hitherto unknown». The precise archival source of each remains to be indicated.

II. Prayers composed from her words — texts composed by others from phrases taken from her writings: the Prayer to Jesus Crucified (booklet by Fr Juan Carlos Silva, FSA) and the Beatitudes of Mother Rosa.

Prayers to Mother Rosa or about her (novenas, acts of entrustment, celebrations), which are not hers, are not included. The «Oração composta pela Bem-aventurada Madre Rosa» translated by Fr Valdo corresponds to nos. 9 and 1.

To the Eternal Father

1. I believe in You, my God, infinite Truth.

I hope in You, my God, infinite Mercy.

I love You, my God, lovable Infinite.

I repent of having offended You, my God,

infinite Goodness.

I resolve to sanctify myself in life and in death with your Sacraments, my God, Infinite Holiness.

My God, grant that I may know You

and know myself…:

You, to love You, praise You,

serve You and glorify You.

Myself, to hate myself, (cf. Lk 14:26-27)

to abhor myself and bring myself to nothing.

My God, my Lord,

enlighten me,

guard me,

bless me,

comfort me,

sanctify me,

inebriate me

with your holy,

divine Love.

2. - Lord, remember.

- Lord, provide.

- Lord, take care of it.

Oh! My Jesus, as you had foretold, and now it is time to draw all the hearts of your daughters. Yes, my dear Jesus, when shall I have the consolation of seeing them all chained to your helm?

May what I ask of you come soon!

3. Eternal Father, ah, give me communion Yourself in this my spiritual communion, giving me your divine Son as You gave Him for the redemption of the human race, so that He may redeem in me all my senses, leaving me wholly free from their slavery; and, chained by your mercy and a slave to your every will, may I remain as I am, and You, in giving me the essence of your love, may I be satisfied with It alone. Father, hand me Jesus with your gentle hand. Yes, sole being of my life, You are my all, for when I possess You, I have everything in You, everything.

4. Prayer to the right hand of the Eternal Father

To the right hand of the Eternal Father, dipped in the blood of Jesus that creates the world.

To the right hand of the Eternal Father, dipped in the blood of Jesus that sanctifies the Church.

To the right hand of the Eternal Father, dipped in the blood of Jesus that glorifies Paradise.

To the right hand of the Eternal Father, which sanctifies Saint Anne to be Mother of the Immaculate.

To the right hand of the Eternal Father, which, dipped in the blood of Jesus, works the Immaculate Conception in the womb of Saint Anne.

To the right hand of the Eternal Father which, dipped in the blood of Jesus, wrought the Incarnation in the womb of Mary.

To the right hand of the Eternal Father, dipped in the blood of Jesus that raises Jesus from the dead.

To the right hand of the Eternal Father, dipped in the blood of Jesus that glorifies, placing Him at its own right in Heaven.

5. For the month of the Eternal Father

Dear Eternal Father, I offer You the blood and the most intense sufferings that your son endured in his left hand while the executioners drove in the nail.

(Glory Be).

Dear Eternal Father, I offer You the blood and the most intense sufferings that your Son endured in his right hand while the executioners drove in the nail.

(Glory Be).

Dear Eternal Father, I offer You the blood and the most intense sufferings that your Son endured in his left foot while the executioners drove in the nail.

(Glory Be).

Dear Eternal Father, I offer You the blood and the most intense sufferings that your Son endured in his right foot while the executioners drove in the nail.

(Glory Be).

Dear Eternal Father, I offer You the blood that flowed from the side of your Son and, through the immense love that moved Him to give His whole self to redeem us, I commend to You Holy Church, poor sinners, and the spiritual and temporal growth of our poor Institute.

(Glory Be).

6. Prayers to Jesus

- Lord, remember

- Lord, provide

- Lord, take care of it.

7. Oh! My Jesus, as you had foretold, and now it is time to draw all the hearts of your daughters. Yes, my dear Jesus, when shall I have the consolation of seeing them all chained to your helm?

May what I ask of you come soon!

8. Jesus, my Bridegroom, my Paradise, […] invest me with your powers: you are infinite and infinite are your powers. Invest me, I am your bride […] and it is only right that, before I go out from here, I be clothed anew by your Spirit in all its fullness, laying aside my own garment, being clothed in yours. Without respite, without rest and caring for nothing, I shall run everywhere, crying out to all; with a voice that is yours I shall pierce hearts and convert all to your feet; I ask nothing else of you […]. After my labours, the refreshment, the joy I desire is to possess you; you know all that I shall need for comfort; I want nothing, you know it, neither of the world nor of Paradise: you alone I want to clasp in my arms.

9. Behold, my Jesus, the heart that in a moment you are to dwell in; I keep it open, waiting for you. Come, my God, my dear one, come, Volcano of love, to set this heart of yours on fire; consume all that you find in it that does not please you; leave it only inebriated with your divine Love!

10. My Love, do not forget, for charity’s sake, but only speak to me and tell me while you are in my heart; let me feel your sweetness, as I clasp you in the inebriation of your most exquisite wine. Ah! why do I never remain drunk with Love! Love alone I want!

I felt what I never had and longed for. If I sinned and was vile, put it all, my Love, behind your back so that you cannot see it. Look only at your creature and never at her misdeeds. Make me beautiful with your graces; so shall I see my Eternal God, your Father, and you, who want everything for Him and long to see Him loved and venerated by all.

11. Dear Jesus, how many graces and benefits and gifts, my Beloved, you will pour into me now that you have come to enclose yourself within this heart of yours…

Ah, my all, satisfy me, for otherwise I die. Ah, you are my joy; ah, rest peacefully, and meanwhile speak to me, for I want to hear your melodious voice: may its sound be of love; yes, I have a million things to tell you… a hunger for your love devours me; tell me that you will soon consume me, and you, my Beloved, point me to the fountain of your side, the open wounds of your breast to drink from, and you say: Come, my beloved bride, put your lips to this heart of mine and here you will find everything […].

12. Consumatus [Consumatum] est

Blessed am I, if I can say on my deathbed: Consumatum est.

My dear love Jesus, this head that is now worn out from having laboured too much for you; my Jesus, through the long vigils and every kind of task, this is how I find myself for you.

These ears that hardly hear any more, from having been wounded for so long by the cries of humanity: this is for you, my Jesus.

These eyes that no longer see, from the continual nights spent writing, working for you, my Jesus.

This mouth that now seems so reluctant to open, it is only because it has no more strength, not having breath enough to form a word, and this from having worn out my lungs speaking, praying for you, my Jesus.

The sense of smell, which has also suffered from the overpowering stench of gangrene: all this for you, my Jesus.

These hands, now without strength to lift them, and this from having used them continually for you, my Jesus.

This breast, now exhausted [?] for you, O my Jesus, from having wearied it continually in every kind of labour and hardship without ever giving it rest; and behold, now it has no strength but the divine, which you, my Jesus, provide me. All for you, my Jesus.

These loins, now weak and giving no more sign of life, and this for you, my Jesus, because, from lying continually in discomfort, they are now more painful than ever, for you, my good Jesus.

These feet and legs that no longer hold me up, this from being continually on my feet, running everywhere, for your works; they have been consumed for you, my Jesus – Consumatum Est.

13. Jesus, consume me with your love; happy shall I be for Eternity.

(Keepsake written in her own hand by my most beloved mother S. A. Rosa Gattorno, in the year 1899)

14. Jesus, my love, let everything be given me by you and wrought in me by you: my little Community I place at your feet; do not let the Dragon ever snatch away a single one: be always our defence, to you I entrust it, you take care of it: my Love, [I ask you,] consume me in your love; nothing else do I want!

Rome, 7 Nov 1887. Your poor M. Rosa (To Sr A. Quintilla?)

15. To the Holy Spirit

Ah! Blazing Volcano, source of my Love, with what delights you have adorned so festive a cavern! The closer I draw, the further I enter, I find neither end nor beginning; I see only a blazing abyss of love which, as it draws near, is consumed and moves. All is Love: the cleansing of sins, the consuming of our vileness…, the countless fountains of grace, it contains all within itself! […].

Holy Spirit, divine Fire, through that outpouring by which, in the conception of the Son of God in the womb of Most Holy Mary, you cooperated in the great mystery of redemption, obtain for us from God the Father what we ask.

16. To Mary

Hail, O Queen, save us, queen, give us refuge, I am your daughter; beneath your virginal mantle receive me, cover my misery, for of mercy you are the treasurer. Ah, upon me pour out abundantly this gift of yours; life you are, and of those who suffer; the sweetness, our hope, yes, with hope fill our minds. God save you, to you we cry, we, the banished children of Eve, you, O star of the sea, O new Eve, who with your foot crushed the enemy. Save us from his insidious temptations; sighing and mourning, to you I raise my faint voice, begging you to grant me to unite these my prayers to yours. O beloved Mother, send them to the Eternal God; oh, where does my thought take flight: if you grant me this, I shall be heard, I shall reach that blessed harbour from this valley of tears. Come then, our advocate, and as advocate go to the judge; tell him everything; turn to us those eyes of yours from paradise, so that our senses, thirsting for its most living light, may remain inebriated, and like an arrow may [it] come to engrave me. After this exile, show us Jesus. Mary, look upon your handmaid who, brought to nothing, is suffering and grieving at the hem of your mantle, all trembling in immense sorrow; ah, hear me, let pity move you, my dearest; you alone can save me, letting me see the face of the Being, of my life, the blessed fruit of your womb. O clement, O loving, offer fervent prayers joined to the splendour of your words; obtain for us the loosing of all those bonds that hold us back, so that we may run after you, O fair hope, comfort of us sinners, way and guide to reach the shore so longed for in such love, that we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ, our Maker and Redeemer.

17. At your feet, O great sovereign, I implore pity and help from you, all confused to see myself appointed to put on you the garments and other gifts that these daughters of yours have offered you. How can I ever clothe you in them, I who am an abyss of corruption, the most wretched and unworthy of these dear daughters? Forgetting everything and clothing you with all these beautiful gifts, I take courage to carry out what they command me. With my forehead to the ground, first give me your blessing, and I, covered by it, set about clothing you.

All this, I know well, O Mary, is nothing, but all together we wish to offer you what I well know you desire. Yes, O our Mother, we offer you our heart, so that it may never again turn even one heartbeat towards other objects besides those that please you, so as to love you and persevere in holy virtue. To you we leave the care of them, and as yours you must keep them, so that they may not depart from your motherly bosom, where one day we may all contemplate you at your feet.

With your help, O Beloved Mother, we shall all come to dwell with you.

18. Oh! Seraphim, send prayers to Mary once more; tell her once more to look upon me, for I am her daughter.

Oh! blessed gaze of love, feed me, for on it alone I want to live, to die.

Oh! Mary, you are the Merciful One, you are the Mother, my mother, because you are the mother of my Creator; with your sweet words tell the Bridegroom that I want to die of love. Within that lily of sharp thorns of love I feel my heart feeding. Tread, angels, upon this treasure [?]: pasture of love is for me alone.

19. To Saint Anne

Most august Matron, cradle of the beneficent seed, nay more, source of every hope, co-worker of the new covenant. Your womb was sanctified by the most holy Trinity, because it was to form the dwelling of the beloved Daughter of the Father, the new Eve. Tell me what your womb felt when there entered it She who was the delight of the Father, and had been filled with the Holy Spirit, and whom the Son of God the Father looked upon as Mother, showing Himself obedient to come down and make Himself small in order to dwell in Her.

(taken from the writings of Blessed Mother Anna Rosa Gattorno — booklet by Fr Juan Carlos Silva, FSA)

O Jesus, Beloved and Crucified,
of you I ask strength and perseverance
to fulfil your divine will.
Inflame me with your sweet love
and help me in all my sorrows and trials.
Pour out upon me the fullness of your choicest blessings.

O Jesus, Beloved and Crucified,
strengthen my spirit;
exchange my will for yours,
be comfort and balm for my wounds,
sweet refreshment that scatters every fear,
on the road that still remains for me to travel.

O Jesus, Beloved and Crucified,
if my bones bend, lift me up
and with the nectar of your love fill me.
From the evil dragon defend me
and with your light enlighten me,
that for You alone I may live and die.
Amen.

It is good to know that we are nothing and that the work is for God and of God.

Blessed are we, if we leave everything in the hands of God, the sole object of our life.

Blessed are we, if with courage we are strong and do not fear!

Blessed are we, if in the heart of Jesus alone we can find true love.

Blessed are we, if we look upon the Crucified One: He will be our strength, our guide, our courage.

Blessed are we, if from the Cross alone we learn to love.

Blessed are we, if truth is our treasure.

Blessed are we, if we receive everything from the hands of God and thank Him for the mercy He shows us.

The love of God is all we need; what remains is nothing and less than nothing.
